headline: Comp sales accelerate as buybacks lift EPS growth
summary_short: O'Reilly grew Q2 FY2026 revenue 8% y/y to $4.89B and diluted EPS 10% y/y to $0.86, as comparable store sales accelerated to 6.0% from 4.1% a year ago.
summary_long: Sales rose 8% y/y to $4.89B on 6.0% comparable store sales growth (up from 4.1% a year ago), with gross margin steady at 51.4% and operating margin steady at 20.2%. Net income grew 7% y/y to $715M while diluted EPS grew faster, up 10% to $0.86, as buybacks cut diluted shares to 829M from 858M. The company repurchased $1.51B of stock in the quarter and $2.43B year-to-date. Long-term debt rose to $7.01B from $5.82B a year ago, funding buybacks and widening the shareholders' deficit to $1.84B. O'Reilly raised full-year comparable store sales guidance to 4.0%-6.0%.

drivers.explanation: Growth came from both professional and DIY channels as the company continued executing its dual-market strategy, per CEO commentary.
Sales growth was driven by 6.0% comparable store sales growth plus 46 net new stores opened during the quarter.
Gross margin held flat at 51.4% of sales as gross profit grew in step with sales, both up 8% y/y.
Operating margin held flat at 20.2% of sales as SG&A grew at the same 8% pace as revenue.
Net income growth of 7% lagged operating income growth of 8%, reflecting higher interest expense as long-term debt rose to $7.01B from $5.82B.
EPS grew faster than net income because diluted share count fell to 829M from 858M following $1.51B of share repurchases in the quarter.
Management raised full-year comparable store sales guidance to 4.0%-6.0%, citing confidence in underlying demand and continued customer-service focus.
